subject: Acme AI — evaluation assets provisioning & MAP
messages:
From: Elena Rossi <elena@acme.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-10T09:15:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Evaluation assets exchange & MAP

Hi Priyom —

Thanks for taking the time last week on the call. Per our discussion, Acme.ai would like to move forward with a short mutual action plan so we can share a subset of our internal testcases and prompt packs for Redwood to run a closed evaluation. High level asks from our side: 

- We need a clear usage agreement: evaluation-only, non‑redistributable, 60-day evaluation window, secure storage, and deletion confirmation after 90 days.
- A timeline showing when Redwood can ingest the assets and return aggregate quality metrics and a short writeup (precision/recall-style signals + failure examples).
- Confirmation of what telemetry/logs Redwood will capture and how long they will be retained.

We can provide: a 2.5k-sample testcase manifest (CSV), a zipped prompt pack (prompts + expected canonical outputs), and a small labeled evaluation set (CSV). Procurement would like an MSA/PO path as well — I’ve looped Marco and procurement in CC.

Can you send a MAP draft and an ingestion/closure timeline? We prefer to get materials into your environment by the week of Nov 22 if possible.

Thanks,
Elena
Elena Rossi
Head of Evaluation Programs, Acme AI
Elena.Rossi@acme.ai

Subject: Re: Evaluation assets exchange & MAP

Hi Elena —

Appreciate the clear asks. I’ve drafted a concise mutual action plan (attached) that maps deliverables, ownership and acceptance criteria. Summary below — I’ll also upload the doc to the shared Drive link.

Proposed MAP highlights:
- Week 0 (Nov 22): Acme delivers sample prompt pack + manifest to our secure intake (S3 w/ KMS).
- Week 1–2: Redwood ingestion and schema validation; security review and generate ingestion report.
- Week 3: Evaluation run with baseline models (public variants we agreed on); produce aggregated quality dashboard + failure examples.
- Week 4: Joint review; iterate on tests if needed; final acceptance or follow-up scope.

Usage constraints (we propose): evaluation-only; no sharing outside Redwood eval team; dataset retention 90 days maximum after final acceptance; deletion receipt provided. If you need stronger constraints (shorter retention, strict air‑gapped handling), say so and we’ll escalate to our private deployment team.

Attachments: MAP_draft_20261110.pdf (MAP with deliverables & sign-off lanes).

Quick question for procurement: does Acme require a countersigned MSA prior to samples, or is a limited-scope NDA/Exhibit sufficient for sample transfer? Our standard practice is to require an evaluation exhibit for small test materials but we can accommodate an MSA if that’s your procurement policy.

Best,
Priyom Das
Senior Sales Manager — Redwood Inference
priyom@redwood.com

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Rossi <elena@acme.ai>, Marco Giordano <marco@acme.ai>
Date: 2026-11-11T10:30:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Evaluation assets exchange & MAP — security/ops notes

Looping in a few operational notes so Acme has visibility into what we’ll do on intake and what we need from them. Priyom — posting here so it’s part of the thread.

- Ingest: We’ll provide a presigned S3 ingest URL tied to a temporary IAM role. Files must be encrypted at rest; we will wrap with our KMS key on receipt.
- Access controls: Only the Redwood Eval team + named SEs will have access to the raw assets. Aggregate metrics and failure examples may be exported to the account-facing dashboard (no raw content).
- Telemetry: We collect request-level latency and per-test pass/fail signals; we do not persist raw prompt text beyond the 90-day retention unless explicitly agreed.
- Compliance artifacts: For procurement, we can provide a redacted ingestion report and a summary SOC2 control mapping for the evaluation folder. If Acme requires on-prem/offline processing, we can propose Redwood Private but that will add ~3–4 weeks to schedule.

Requesting from Acme before ingest: a named list of individuals who should have access, and confirmation of retention window (we proposed 90 days). If procurement needs stricter language we should get that now.

Ben Carter
Principal Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.com

From: Elena Rossi <elena@acme.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
Cc: Marco Giordano <marco@acme.ai>, Acme AI Procurement <procure@acme.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-12T08:07:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Evaluation assets exchange & MAP — confirmation

Thanks — this looks good. Procurement confirms a signed limited-scope Exhibit (attached MSA bundle) will be sufficient for the sample transfer; we don’t need a full countersigned enterprise MSA before ingest. We will: 

- Deliver the manifest + prompt pack by COB Nov 22. Attached is a small manifest and a list of named reviewers.
- Accept the 90-day retention with the requirement that Redwood sends a deletion confirmation email when assets are removed.
- Require a redacted ingestion report and a short summary of SOC2 mappings as Ben described.

We’d like a final Go/No-Go by Nov 19 from Redwood — that gives us time to route the Exhibit through procurement.

Elena
